keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: When set, the keyed upsert is applied one dataset at a time, partitioned by this column's distinct values in ascending order: staging is first deduplicated to one row per (dataset, key), then each dataset's UPDATE-then-INSERT runs against the target as the prior datasets left it, so a business key recurring across datasets ends at the value from the last dataset carrying it. Generated by UpsertGenerator.GenerateDataSetLoopStatement as one combined script (UpsertGenerator.cs:184-186,368-554) instead of separate UPDATE/INSERT statements, reporting its Inserts/Updates totals as one result-set row. Consumed as UpsertOptions.DataSetColumn, set from 'MapNameOrNull(nameMap, flow.Load.DataSetColumn) ?? flow.Load.DataSetColumn' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:923-925), i.e. mapped to the cleaned target column name when column-name cleanup renamed it. Distinct from the similarly named source.dataSetColumn (IngestionEndpointYaml.DataSetColumn), which instead feeds the canonical dataset index on a newly-created target (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:365) and is unrelated to this upsert-loop behavior. Honors load.batchUpsert/load.batchUpsertRowCount within each dataset iteration. Has no effect on a keyless flow. The YAML value is trimmed and blank-normalized to null at load time ('string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(y.DataSetColumn) ? null : y.DataSetColumn.Trim()', YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:245), unlike most other optional strings in this document (confirmed via YamlDocumentParts.NullIfBlank, which blank-checks but does not trim).
keys.validation: "A dataset-column load (DataSetColumn) cannot be combined with SCD2 versioning." (UpsertGenerator.cs:156, when versioning.scd2.enabled is also true) and "DataSetColumn '<value>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:161, when the possibly name-mapped value does not case-insensitively match a bulk-copied target column name). Both are run-time checks raised when the upsert is generated, not at YAML load time.

keys.description: Keeps the run-scoped staging table after a SUCCESSFUL run instead of dropping it (a FAILED run always keeps its staging table for debugging, regardless of this flag). Consumed directly at IngestionFlowRunner.cs:522 ('if (!flow.Load.KeepStagingTable)'): when false (the default), both the staging table and, if the key-match pass ran, its run-scoped key table are dropped with 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...' after a successful run; when true, the staging table is left in place (optionally truncated, see load.truncateStagingOnCompletion) and the match-key table is also left undropped.

Business key column names (as they appear among the bulk-copied SOURCE columns) that identify a row for the update/insert match. Consumed as IngestionLoadPolicy.KeyColumns (IngestionPolicies.cs:12). Whenever this list is non-empty (and not overridden, see matchKeys.keyColumns), it becomes the 'effective key' (IngestionFlowRunner.EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820) used everywhere a business key is needed: the schema-evolution critical-mismatch gate, where a key, hash-key, identity, or primary-key column with an incompatible type change is flagged CRITICAL rather than silently widened (passed as 'KeySet(EffectiveKeyColumns(flow))' at IngestionFlowRunner.cs:340 into SchemaEvolutionPlanner.IsCritical, SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs:112-115, independently confirmed: IsCritical returns true for a HashKey/Identity-role column, a primary-key column, or any column named in the key set); the two-step upsert's key-equality join and its per-row change-detection scope (UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements, passed verbatim as UpsertOptions.KeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:906); and, name-mapped to target column names via the bulk-copy column map, the canonical key index built on a newly-created target and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, its filtered-unique SCD2 key-index variant (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:359-369,378-393). An empty list routes the flow through the keyless insert-all path instead (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:853-857), which ignores skipUpdateExisting/skipInsertNew/batchUpsert*/dataSetColumn entirely and always appends every staged row.
keys.validation: Load time: "'<source>': 'versioning.scd2' requires 'load.keyColumns' (the business key the dimension versions by)." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:123-131, when versioning.scd2.enabled is true and this list is empty). Run time: "MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget is on, but the flow has no key columns (set load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:669-671, when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and the effective key list is empty). Also run time, at upsert generation: "An upsert requires at least one key column." (UpsertGenerator.cs:135, unreachable via YAML because the keyless path is taken first when this list is empty) and "Key column '<key>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:143, when an entry does not case-insensitively match a bulk-copied target column name; this list is passed to the upsert as-is, never name-mapped, so it can diverge from cleaned target names).

keys.description: Turns on the post-load key-match (deleted-row detection) pass: after the upsert, the full distinct SOURCE key set is landed in a run-scoped table and anti-joined against the target, so a target row whose key no longer exists in the source is tagged or deleted per matchKeys.action (IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, invoked at IngestionFlowRunner.cs:463 only when this flag is true). It also selects which key columns are 'effective' everywhere a business key is used: when true and matchKeys.keyColumns is non-empty, matchKeys.keyColumns overrides load.keyColumns for the upsert, the schema-evolution key set, and the canonical/SCD2 index planning (EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820); otherwise load.keyColumns is used regardless of this flag. At YAML load time, when this is true and matchKeys.action resolves to Tag (its default), the loader force-enables systemColumns.deletedDate to true even if the YAML explicitly set it to false (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:140-145; pinned by test YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.TagMode_AutoEnableOverridesExplicitFalseOnDeletedDate, confirmed to exist in tests/SqlFlow.Core.Tests/YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.cs), because Tag mode's soft delete stamps DeletedDate_DW.
keys.validation: This flag itself has no load-time validation; it gates the run-time checks described under load.keyColumns and systemColumns.deletedDate ("MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget is on, but the flow has no key columns ..." and "MatchKeys Tag mode soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW; enable the DeletedDate_DW system column.", both in IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:669-677).

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: Omits the INSERT branch of the keyed upsert: only existing matched rows are updated, new keys are never appended. Consumed as UpsertOptions.SkipInsert (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:908), gating the INSERT statement in UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements ('if (!options.SkipInsert)', UpsertGenerator.cs:218). Ignored entirely on a keyless flow: BuildInsertAll (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952) always inserts every staged row regardless of this flag. Ignored when versioning.scd2 is enabled (its insert-new-version statement always runs; SkipInsert does not apply, per the UpsertOptions doc comment at UpsertGenerator.cs:95).

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (load.keyColumns or matchKeys.keyColumns non-empty)
keys.description: Omits the UPDATE branch of the keyed upsert: matched rows are never rewritten, only new keys are inserted. Consumed as UpsertOptions.SkipUpdate (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:907), gating the UPDATE statement in UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements ('if (!options.SkipUpdate && nonKey.Count > 0)', UpsertGenerator.cs:192) and the equivalent branch inside the dataset-partitioned loop script. The UPDATE branch is also naturally skipped whenever every data column is a key column, independent of this flag. Ignored entirely on a keyless flow, which has no update branch at all, and ignored when versioning.scd2 is enabled, whose close/insert statements do not consult SkipUpdate (UpsertOptions doc comment, UpsertGenerator.cs:95).

Accepted and stored verbatim on IngestionLoadPolicy.StreamData (IngestionPolicies.cs:38-40, whose doc comment states 'When false the engine buffers in memory and writes on Threads parallel writers'), but not read anywhere in IngestionFlowRunner: every bulk-copy path (BulkCopyAsync, BulkCopyInitLoadAsync, StreamSelectToStagingAsync; IngestionFlowRunner.cs:954-1042) always streams the source SqlDataReader directly into a single SqlBulkCopy regardless of this flag's value, and the buffered/parallel-writer alternative the model's doc comment describes is not implemented in this runner (confirmed by a solution-wide search: '.StreamData' is only ever written, never read, outside the YAML DTO, the mapped policy record, and the legacy/full-mode row equivalents). Setting it to false only changes what is recorded on the mapped IngestionLoadPolicy, with no observable effect on how a YAML-loaded flow actually runs.

keys.default: null (unset); the one consumer treats null the same as 1 (sequential)
keys.appliesWhen: initLoad.enabled is true (the InitLoad backfill's segment fan-out); unused otherwise
keys.description: Parallel reader/writer count. Consumed only by the InitLoad backfill path: BulkCopyInitLoadAsync computes 'var maxDegree = Math.Max(1, load.Threads ?? 1);' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:984) and fans its per-segment bulk copies out across a SemaphoreSlim gate of that size; the normal (non-InitLoad) incremental/full read always uses a single connection with no concurrency, so this setting has no effect outside initLoad.enabled: true. Also recorded verbatim on the run-log record for observability (IngestionRunRecord.Threads, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1219). At YAML load time only a strictly positive value survives: 'Threads = y.Threads is > 0 ? y.Threads : null' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:247), so 0 or a negative value is silently normalized to null (the same 'engine default' outcome as leaving it unset).

keys.appliesWhen: load.keepStagingTable is true
keys.description: When the staging table is kept after a successful run (load.keepStagingTable: true), truncates it instead of leaving its rows, so the kept table carries structure without the run's data (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:542-548: 'TRUNCATE TABLE ...' when true, otherwise an info log that it was kept with its data). Has no effect when load.keepStagingTable is false: the default branch drops the table outright, which already discards the data, so this flag never fires there.

keys.default: { action: tag, keyColumns: [], thresholdPercent: 20, ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths: null, dateColumn: null, sourceFilter: null, targetFilter: null }
keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (otherwise parsed and stored but the pass never runs)
keys.description: Optional block configuring the deleted-row detection (key-match) pass: the tag-vs-delete action, the threshold guard, the age-based ignore window, and the key/filter overrides. Binds to IngestionMatchKeysYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapMatchKeys to SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.MatchKeyPolicy (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:253-291); absent and present-but-empty both produce the same defaults. The block only takes runtime effect when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:463); its default Tag action still influences the systemColumns.deletedDate auto-enable at load time even with no explicit matchKeys.action, whenever load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is set (see load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget).

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: What to do with a target row whose key vanished from the source: 'tag' soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW (and RowStatus_DW 'D' when systemColumns.rowStatus is on), leaving the row in place; 'delete' hard-deletes the row. Consumed by MatchKeyGenerator.Generate to choose between the UPDATE-stamp statement and the DELETE statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:99-120). Tag mode (whether authored explicitly or left at its default) also drives two other behaviors: at YAML load time, if load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is also true, systemColumns.deletedDate is force-enabled to true regardless of what the YAML said (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:142-145); and at run time, only Tag mode reconciles resurrections, where a previously tagged row whose key reappears in the source is un-tagged (DeletedDate_DW cleared, RowStatus_DW reset to 'U') independent of the threshold guard (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:124-141). Delete mode ignores matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths entirely: the age-window predicate is only built in the Tag branch (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:104-110).
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.action' must be 'tag' or 'delete', got '<value>'." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:264-265), matched by trimming and uppercasing the raw value with no dash/underscore stripping (there being no multi-word spelling to strip); null/absent defaults to Tag without erroring.

keys.default: null; at run time (non-YAML flows only) falls back to incremental.dateColumn
keys.appliesWhen: matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths is set
keys.description: The target date column bounding the ignore-after-months window (see matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths). Only read at run time when that setting is present: IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync resolves 'policy.DateColumn ?? flow.Incremental.DateColumn' and maps the chosen name to its bulk-copied target spelling via the source-to-target column map (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:682-685); for a YAML-loaded flow the incremental.dateColumn fallback is never actually exercised, because the loader's load-time validation (see matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths) already guarantees this field is set whenever it would be needed.
keys.validation: The name is resolved through the same MapName helper used for key columns, so a value naming an ignored or virtual column (one not among the bulk-copied target columns) fails with "Key column '<name>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161); the generic message text is reused here even though this is a date column, not a business key.

keys.default: null (no age window: the tag action applies to every candidate row regardless of age)
keys.appliesWhen: matchKeys.action resolves to tag; silently ignored in delete mode
keys.description: In Tag mode, restricts the tag action to target rows whose matchKeys.dateColumn value is within this many months of now: the generated candidate predicate adds 'AND trg.[dateColumn] >= DATEADD(MONTH, -{months}, SYSUTCDATETIME())' (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:107-110), so older rows are left untouched (neither tagged nor counted as candidates). Ignored in Delete mode: the Delete branch never builds this predicate at all (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:99-103), so setting this alongside matchKeys.action: delete has no effect and raises no error.
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths' requires 'matchKeys.dateColumn'." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:277-278, load time, whenever this is set and matchKeys.dateColumn is blank, checked before Tag/Delete mode is even known, and regardless of load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget). Two further run-time checks exist for non-YAML-built flows, otherwise unreachable via YAML because the load-time check already guarantees a dateColumn: MatchKeyGenerator.Generate's "IgnoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths requires a date column." (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:89) and IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync's "matchKeys.ignoreDeletedRowsAfterMonths requires matchKeys.dateColumn (or an incremental dateColumn)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:682-684), the latter of which would otherwise fall back to flow.Incremental.DateColumn.

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true (otherwise parsed and stored but never read: the check is 'flow.Load.MatchKeysInSourceAndTarget && flow.MatchKeys.KeyColumns.Count > 0', and C#'s && short-circuits, so the property is never even accessed when the flag is false)
keys.description: Overrides load.keyColumns for the whole flow, not just the delete-detection comparison, whenever load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and this list is non-empty: EffectiveKeyColumns(flow) prefers matchKeys.keyColumns over load.keyColumns in that case (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820), and that effective key set is what the keyed upsert, the schema-evolution critical-mismatch gate, and the canonical/SCD2 index planning all use (see load.keyColumns for the exact consumers and citations), so setting this also changes the business key the upsert matches on, not only which rows the key-match pass considers deleted. When load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is false, this list is parsed and stored but has no effect anywhere.
keys.validation: The same downstream checks as load.keyColumns apply to the resolved effective list: "Key column '<key>' is not among the data columns." (UpsertGenerator.cs:143) and "Key column '<source>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161, for canonical/SCD2 index name-mapping).

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: A predicate, raw-append contract (authored with its own leading ' AND '), bounding the SOURCE rows read to build the 'still present' key set for the delete-detection pass. IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync resolves it as 'policy.SourceFilter, else flow.Source.Filter' (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:704, trimmed at the point of use), so an unset matchKeys.sourceFilter reuses the flow's own source.filter, meaning rows the load itself never reads are, by default, not wrongly treated as deleted. The key scan this bounds is a fresh 'SELECT DISTINCT ...' over the full source (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:706-710) and deliberately never applies the incremental window, so a row outside the current run's incremental read is still correctly recognized as present in the source.

keys.default: null (no restriction on the candidate/action/resurrect statements; the total-row count is never restricted by this field regardless of its value)
keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: CORRECTED: A predicate, raw-append contract (authored with its own leading ' AND '), bounding which TARGET rows the key-match pass may count as a candidate or act on. MatchKeyGenerator.Generate appends the trimmed filter (captured once at MatchKeyGenerator.cs:95) to three places: the candidate-count query (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:148), the tag/delete action statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:102 for Delete mode, :119 for Tag mode), and, in Tag mode only, the resurrect statement (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:139). It is NOT applied to the target's TOTAL-row count, which is the threshold's denominator: 'SELECT @Total = COUNT_BIG(*) FROM {trg};' (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:147) counts the whole target table unconditionally, with no targetFilter, no candidatePredicates, and not even a 'trg' alias. Practical consequence: when targetFilter narrows the pass to a subset of the target, the reported/enforced breach percentage (@Candidates * 100.0 / @Total) is candidates-within-the-filtered-subset divided by the WHOLE unfiltered target's row count, not the filtered subset's size, so a targetFilter that scopes to a small slice of a large table makes even a total wipeout of that slice register as a small percentage and can silently slip under matchKeys.thresholdPercent.

keys.appliesWhen: load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true
keys.description: Skips the tag/delete action (and reports it) when more than this percentage of the target would be affected. MatchKeyGenerator's generated script computes '@Candidates * 100.0 / @Total > {threshold}' and, when breached, sets @Breached and skips the action statement entirely while still reporting @Total/@Candidates (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:146-158). The comparison is only evaluated when the target has at least one row (@Total > 0), so an empty target can never breach. Resurrection (un-tagging a reappeared key) is independent of this threshold and always runs when applicable. A breach is surfaced as a warning-level log line by IngestionFlowRunner.RunMatchKeysAsync, not a run failure (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:729-736).
keys.validation: "'<source>': 'matchKeys.thresholdPercent' must be 0 to 100, got <value>." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:271-272, load time). The same range is re-checked defensively at run time by MatchKeyGenerator.Generate: "ActionThresholdPercent must be 0 to 100, got {value}." (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:79), reachable only from a flow assembled outside the YAML loader.

keys.default: null (unset); FlowId is then 0 and SysAlias is null
keys.description: The flow's display name. Unlike the file flow (where 'name' is required), it is optional for an ing document. When non-blank it is trimmed (`y.Name.Trim()`, YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:100) and becomes IngestionFlow.SysAlias verbatim (legacy flw.Ingestion.SysAlias), and it seeds IngestionFlow.FlowId via YamlDocumentParts.StableFlowId: the trimmed name is hashed into the same name-based RFC4122 v5 GUID the file flow uses (FlowIdentity.FromName, confirmed a SHA-1 name-based v5 UUID over a fixed namespace constant), and BitConverter.ToInt32 of the GUID's first four bytes, masked with 0x7FFFFFFF (clearing the sign bit), yields a stable non-negative int32 -- because unlike the file flow's GUID identity, the legacy flw.Ingestion.FlowID column (and this model's FlowId) is a plain int. A blank or missing name yields SysAlias = null and FlowId = 0 (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:149-150). FlowId is not just informational: IngestionFlowRunner names the run-scoped staging table `stg_{flow.FlowId}_{stamp}_{runToken}` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:161) and the match-key table `mkey_{flow.FlowId}_{stamp}_{runToken}` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:469), and stamps FlowId on the run-log record (BuildRunRecord, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1204). SysAlias, when set, appears in the run-start log line and otherwise falls back to the target table name there (`flow.SysAlias ?? flow.Target.Table.Name`, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:208), and is also stamped on the run-log record (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1208).

keys.default: { sync: true, cleanColumnNames: false, cleanColumnNameRegex: null, replaceInvalidCharsWith: null, convertUnicodeToNonUnicode: false, allowTableRewrite: false } (MapSchema produces these defaults even when the whole block is absent)
keys.description: Optional schema-synchronization block for the ing document: distinct from, and much simpler than, the file-flow document's schema block (no evolve/defaultColumnType/overrides keys here). Bound from IngestionYaml.Schema and mapped by MapSchema (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:324-340) onto IngestionFlow.SchemaSync (SchemaSyncPolicy). Consumed by IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build, which always runs (for both the staging and target desired-schema passes) regardless of sync, and by IngestionFlowRunner's target-evolution step, which runs only when sync is true (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:334-355).

Opt-in for an expensive table-rewrite ALTER (for example widening int to bigint) on the TARGET table. Consulted only inside the schema.sync evolution call against the target (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:341); the staging-table evolution call earlier in the same run hardcodes allowTableRewrite: false regardless of this setting (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:266). RewritePolicy.Decide maps false to RewriteHandling.RequireOptIn (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/RewritePolicy.cs:20-21); EvolutionDdlGenerator.Generate then refuses the whole evolution plan before generating any DDL whenever the plan needs a rewrite and the policy requires opt-in (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:31-34).
keys.appliesWhen: schema.sync is true (the target evolution call this governs runs only inside that gate)
keys.validation: When a plan needs a table rewrite and this is false: SchemaRewriteNotPermittedException "Schema evolution on '<target>' requires a table rewrite on column(s) <columns> (for example int to bigint). This holds a table lock for the full rewrite and is refused by default. Set AllowTableRewrite to run it, ideally in a maintenance window." (src/SqlFlow.Core/SchemaRewriteNotPermittedException.cs:12-14, thrown from src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:33).

keys.default: null; DefaultColumnNameCleaner falls back to the canonical legacy pattern [^a-zA-Z0-9æøåÆØÅ_] (LegacyColumnCleanup.DefaultCleanupRegex) when blank
keys.description: Regex whose matches in a raw source column name are replaced (or removed) during the relational sync cleanup. Consulted only when schema.cleanColumnNames is true; blank/absent falls back to the canonical legacy default, which keeps ASCII letters, digits, underscore, and the six Norwegian letters æøåÆØÅ, reproducing the legacy flw.SysCFG.ColCleanupSQLRegExp config default (DefaultColumnNameCleaner.cs:27-32; LegacyColumnCleanup.cs:28-33). This relational-sync cleaner is distinct from, and independently configurable from, the always-on file-flow header cleanup (LegacyColumnCleanup.CleanFileColumnNames), which never consults this key.
keys.appliesWhen: schema.cleanColumnNames is true; ignored otherwise
keys.validation: An invalid regex throws SqlFlowException "Invalid CleanColumnNameRegex '<pattern>': <message>" when DefaultColumnNameCleaner compiles it (a 2-second regex timeout is applied) (DefaultColumnNameCleaner.cs:34-42).

keys.description: Enables source-column-name cleanup for the relational sync path (legacy SMOHelper.CleanupColumnName), opt-in unlike the file-flow header cleanup, which always runs. When true, DefaultColumnNameCleaner.Clean (the sole IColumnNameCleaner implementation, constructed directly by IngestionFlowRunner, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:240) applies cleanColumnNameRegex (or the legacy default pattern) to every raw source column name, replacing matches per replaceInvalidCharsWith, turning a fully-matched (now-empty) name into the literal placeholder 'EmptyColumnName', and de-duplicating case-insensitive collisions with a numeric suffix (DefaultColumnNameCleaner.cs:17-60). The cleaned names become BOTH the staging and target column names (IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build computes them once and both passes reuse the result), so cleanup is not itself gated by schema.sync. When false (the default), raw source names pass through unchanged.

When true, every bulk-copied source column's SQL type is passed through UnicodeConverter.ToNonUnicode while building the desired schema (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:52): nvarchar becomes varchar, nchar becomes char, ntext becomes text (its length cleared), and sysname becomes varchar(128); every other type, including already-non-Unicode text and non-text types, passes through unchanged (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UnicodeConverter.cs:10-22). Designed for SAP Open Hub sources, which type all text as NVARCHAR. Applied unconditionally by IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build (used for both the staging and target desired schemas), so it is not gated by schema.sync.

keys.default: null, which DefaultColumnNameCleaner treats as an empty string (matched characters are removed rather than replaced), DefaultColumnNameCleaner.cs:44
keys.description: Replacement text substituted for each character schema.cleanColumnNameRegex (or the built-in default pattern) matches in a raw column name, via Regex.Replace (DefaultColumnNameCleaner.cs:44,50).
keys.appliesWhen: schema.cleanColumnNames is true; ignored otherwise

keys.description: Gates whether the target table's schema is created or evolved on this run. When true (the default), IngestionFlowRunner calls schemaSync.EvolveAsync against the target with the desired column list, creating the table if it is missing or ALTER-adding new source columns (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:334-355); when false, that call is skipped entirely, so a first run against a non-existent target never creates it (the subsequent load statements would then fail against a table SQL Server cannot find) and new source columns are never propagated onto an existing target. Because targetCreated is only ever set true inside this same gate, a false sync also skips the automatic canonical-index creation and desired-index application that otherwise follow a table-creating run. Only the TARGET-side evolution is gated: the run-scoped staging table is always created (schemaSync.EvolveAsync runs unconditionally for it, with allowTableRewrite hardcoded false, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:266), and column-name cleanup (cleanColumnNames) and unicode conversion (convertUnicodeToNonUnicode) run unconditionally inside IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build, whose single result feeds both the staging and target passes.

The source endpoint: what the flow reads. Binds to the same IngestionEndpointYaml DTO as 'target' (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/IngestionYaml.cs:42-66) and maps to the required IngestionSource on IngestionFlow.Source. This unit (ing-base) covers only this block's presence/requiredness and the 'object'/'table' three-part-name resolution (see source.object, source.table) plus source.dataSetColumn's role in canonical indexing. Connection routing ('server' / 'connection' / 'provider', resolved via the shared YamlDocumentParts.ResolveEndpointConnection) is documented in the connections unit; the read-shaping refinements 'filter', 'filterIsAppend', 'incrementalClause', and 'ignoreColumns' (see IngestionSource, src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionFlow.cs:5-20) are out of this unit's scope; verified their actual behavior (combining with the incremental watermark, and with the InitLoad backfill predicate) is implemented in src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IncrementalWindowResolver.cs and src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/InitLoadPlanner.cs, neither of which is one of this unit's assigned files. The resolved connection's reference is exposed as IngestionSource.ConnectionReference ('@' plus the resolved server alias), consumed by IngestionFlowRunner.cs:165 to open the actual connection.
keys.validation: Missing block throws FlowValidationException "<source>: 'source' is required." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:87), where <source> is the document path passed to LoadFile/Parse (or '<inline>') -- not the YAML 'source:' key itself.

keys.appliesWhen: source.server is not set (exactly one of source.server or source.connection is required)
keys.description: An inline connection string or a ${env:...}/${keyvault:...} reference for the database the ingestion reads from, used when the connection is not already declared under connections:. Resolved the same way as source.server, registering a new connection under the synthetic name 'source'.
keys.validation: Same mutually-exclusive and missing-connection messages as source.server.

keys.default: null (unset); no NCI_DataSetColumn canonical index is planned

The source's three-part relational object name, Database.Schema.Table (or Database.Table for MySQL-style sources; see below). Resolved by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.ParseObject (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:209-228), shared verbatim between source and target -- only the 'section' label ('source' or 'target') differs. Resolution order: 'object' wins over the 'table' alias (see source.table); whichever is non-blank is then, when it contains no '[' at all, checked for the MySQL two-part convention: a plain (unbracketed) two-segment name 'X.Y' (both segments non-empty after `Split('.', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries)`) is expanded to 'X.X.Y', treating the database part as also the schema (natural for MySQL, which has no separate schema level). The (possibly-expanded) string is then parsed by RelationalObject.Parse (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/RelationalObject.cs:20-48): it splits on '.' while respecting [bracketed] identifiers (IngestionText.SplitRespectingBrackets, confirmed bracket-depth-aware with an inner ']' escaped as ']]'), trims and unbrackets each segment (IngestionText.Unbracket), and takes the RIGHTMOST three segments as Database/Schema/Name -- so a name with more than three dotted segments (for example a stray leading server part) silently drops everything left of the third-from-last segment rather than failing. The result becomes IngestionSource.Table (a RelationalObject), whose QualifiedName renders back out as '[Database].[Schema].[Name]' with any ']' doubled inside identifiers.

(RelationalObject.cs:42-44).

Binds to IngestionSystemColumnsYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapSystemColumns to SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.SystemColumnsPolicy (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:308-322); absent and present-but-empty both apply the legacy defaults (Inserted and Updated on, Deleted and RowStatus off). After mapping, deletedDate can be silently force-enabled by the loader when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and matchKeys.action resolves to Tag, overriding even an explicit 'deletedDate: false' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:140-145; see systemColumns.deletedDate).

Consumed as MatchKeyScriptOptions.DeletedDateColumn ('DeletedDate_DW' when true, else null, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:721). Cross-cutting load-time override: when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is true and matchKeys.action resolves to Tag (its default), YamlIngestionFlowLoader force-enables this to true regardless of the authored value; an explicit 'deletedDate: false' is silently overridden (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:140-145, pinned by test YamlIngestionMatchKeysTests.TagMode_AutoEnableOverridesExplicitFalseOnDeletedDate). The run-time requirement below is therefore only reachable for a flow assembled outside the YAML loader, where matchKeysInSourceAndTarget and Tag mode are set without this column enabled.

(MatchKeyGenerator.cs:82-85, when matchKeys.action is Tag and this is false) and, equivalently, "MatchKeys Tag mode soft-deletes by stamping DeletedDate_DW; enable the DeletedDate_DW system column." (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:673-677, the runner's own pre-check before generating the script).

keys.description: CORRECTED: Injects a nullable datetime2(3) InsertedDate_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddSystemColumns, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:91). On a keyed flow it is stamped SYSUTCDATETIME() on every INSERT (UpsertGenerator.cs:222-226) and, on the UPDATE branch, back-filled with SYSUTCDATETIME() only for a matched row whose existing value is NULL (a row that predates the column); otherwise its existing value is preserved ('CASE WHEN trg.[...] IS NULL THEN SYSUTCDATETIME() ELSE trg.[...] END', UpsertGenerator.cs:568-574, legacy parity). On a KEYLESS flow (insert-all), it is the ONLY system column ever stamped: BuildInsertAll only checks 'system.InsertedDate' and stamps SYSUTCDATETIME() on insert; it does not accept or stamp UpdatedDate_DW or RowStatus_DW at all, even when those are enabled (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952). When versioning.scd2 is enabled, the SCD2 insert-new-version statement stamps it with the shared as-of instant on every brand-new/changed version it inserts (UpsertGenerator.cs:338-342). Separately, the SCD2 backfill statement (which runs first, and touches only PRE-EXISTING TARGET rows whose period columns are still NULL, via 'UPDATE trg SET ... FROM {trg} AS trg WHERE trg.[ValidTo] IS NULL', with no staging/source ('src') reference anywhere in that statement, UpsertGenerator.cs:297-303) uses that same target row's own existing InsertedDate_DW value, when present, as its inferred ValidFrom, falling back to the 1900-01-01 epoch sentinel otherwise (UpsertGenerator.cs:294-296); this is the pre-existing TARGET row's own value, not a 'source row's' value.

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (never populated on a keyless flow even when enabled)
keys.description: Injects a nullable char(1) RowStatus_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:94), a per-row action code the engine stamps: 'I' on insert and 'U' on update (UpsertGenerator's insert branch and UpdateSetClauses, UpsertGenerator.cs:231,576-578); 'D' when the key-match pass tags a row deleted and 'U' again when it resurrects a previously tagged row (MatchKeyGenerator.cs:115,131); and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, 'U' when an SCD2 version is closed and 'I' when its replacement version is inserted (UpsertGenerator.cs:316-318,344-347). Consumed as UpsertOptions.RowStatusColumn / MatchKeyScriptOptions.RowStatusColumn ('RowStatus_DW' when true, else null). Like systemColumns.updatedDate, only meaningfully stamped on a KEYED flow; a keyless flow's insert-all statement never references RowStatus_DW, so on a keyless flow the column is added to the schema when enabled but is never populated.

keys.appliesWhen: a keyed flow (never populated on a keyless flow even when enabled)
keys.description: Injects a nullable datetime2(3) UpdatedDate_DW column onto the target (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:92). Stamped SYSUTCDATETIME() only on the keyed upsert's UPDATE branch (UpsertGenerator.UpdateSetClauses, UpsertGenerator.cs:563-565) and, when versioning.scd2 is enabled, on the SCD2 close-of-current-version statement (UpsertGenerator.cs:308-312). It is never set on insert, so a freshly inserted row's UpdatedDate_DW stays NULL until it is later updated. A keyless flow's insert-all statement (BuildInsertAll, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:940-952) never references UpdatedDate_DW at all, so on a keyless flow the column is still added to the schema when enabled but is never populated by any statement the engine generates.

The target endpoint: where the flow writes. Binds to the same IngestionEndpointYaml DTO as 'source' and maps to the required IngestionTarget on IngestionFlow.Target. As with 'source', this unit covers this block's presence/requiredness, the 'object'/'table' three-part-name resolution, 'identityColumn', 'truncateBeforeLoad', and the canonical-index-related 'columnStoreIndex' flag. Connection routing is documented in the connections unit -- the resolved connection must additionally be SQL Server (mssql or azdb), enforced by the shared YamlDocumentParts.RequireSqlServerConnection helper (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:95), because staging, schema evolution, and the upsert are all T-SQL; that check and its message are out of this unit's scope. 'desiredIndexes' is explicitly excluded from this unit (documented in the shared unit) and is likewise out of scope here.

keys.description: Requests a clustered columnstore index on the target, bound to IngestionTarget.ColumnStoreIndex (legacy 'ColumnStoreIndexOnTrg'). This is the main entry point into canonical index behavior: on the run that CREATEs the target table (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:359, gated by `if (targetCreated)`, itself only reachable when schema sync is enabled), IngestionFlowRunner calls CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:17-68), which emits, over the freshly-created (still-empty) table, all of the following as idempotent `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.indexes ...) CREATE ...` statements with stable, non-hashed names: (1) 'NCI_KeyColumn', a UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED index on the flow's effective key columns (load.keyColumns, overridden by matchKeys.keyColumns when the key-match pass is active -- both out of this unit's scope; confirmed via EffectiveKeyColumns, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820), only when there is at least one key column AND SCD2 is not enabled; (2) 'NCI_DateColumn', a plain NONCLUSTERED index on incremental.dateColumn (out of scope), only when that column is set and maps to a real bulk-copied target column; (3) 'NCI_DataSetColumn' (see source.dataSetColumn); (4) 'NCI_UpdatedDate_DW', a plain NONCLUSTERED index on UpdatedDate_DW, only when the desired schema carries that column (systemColumns.updatedDate, out of scope); and (5), only when THIS flag is true AND the desired schema has no identity primary key (see target.identityColumn), a clustered columnstore index named 'CCSI_' followed by the target table's own name with every character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore stripped (CanonicalIndexPlanner.Sanitize, CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:61,137-138). A REQUIRED key column that does not resolve to a real bulk-copied target column (for example because it is in source.ignoreColumns or is a virtual column) FAILS THE RUN with SqlFlowException "Key column '<source>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.MapName, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161); the optional date/dataset columns instead silently produce no index when unmappable (MapNameOrNull, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1165-1166), never failing the run. Separately from this once-at-creation Plan(), whenever versioning.scd2.enabled is true (out of scope), CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements runs on EVERY run, not only at creation (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393): it drops any pre-existing 'NCI_KeyColumn' (or any other non-filtered unique nonclustered index whose columns exactly match the key columns) and creates a FILTERED unique index 'NCI_KeyColumn ... WHERE [<currentFlagColumn>] = 1' instead, because under SCD2 the business key is unique only among current rows -- this is how turning SCD2 on for an already-created table migrates its key index. All of the above map column names using SOURCE names as declared on the flow through the bulk-copy name map to the cleaned TARGET names before building any statement.

keys.description: Name of a computed IDENTITY primary-key column added to the DESIRED TARGET schema only -- never to the run-scoped staging table, since IngestionFlowRunner always builds the target schema with `IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build(sourceColumns, flow, forStaging: false)` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:240), and IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddIdentity runs only `if (!forStaging)` (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:81-84); the staging table's own columns are instead derived directly from the bulk-copied source columns and never carry this column. When blank, AddIdentity is a no-op. When non-blank and no existing desired column already has that name (case-insensitive), AddIdentity appends a new column: SQL type 'int', NOT NULL, Role=Identity, IsIdentity=true, IsPrimaryKey=true (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:129-146); when a column of that name already exists (for example a same-named source column), AddIdentity silently skips adding it -- the existing column is left exactly as inferred/authored and is NOT retrofitted with identity/primary-key semantics. Only the target-table CREATE path actually renders identity/primary-key SQL: EvolutionDdlGenerator.CreateTableStatement adds a `CONSTRAINT [PK_<table>] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (...)` over every column flagged IsPrimaryKey (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:79-84), and ColumnDefinition appends ' IDENTITY(1, 1)' to a column flagged IsIdentity (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:100); the additive ALTER path used against an already-existing table (ColumnsToAdd) always renders a plain nullable column with neither clause (EvolutionDdlGenerator.cs:52-60). Confirmed (by reading SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs, one file outside this unit's assigned list) that this ALTER path is genuinely reachable for identityColumn: SchemaEvolutionPlanner.Plan puts any desired column absent from the existing table's columns, including a newly-declared identityColumn, into ColumnsToAdd purely by name lookup (SchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs:34-38), with no special-casing for identity/PK columns. So declaring identityColumn against a target that already exists without it DOES add the column on the next run, just always as a plain nullable column, never retrofitted with identity/primary-key semantics. The column's presence also feeds canonical-index planning: IngestionFlowRunner computes `hasIdentityPrimaryKey: targetSchema.Columns.Any(c => c.IsPrimaryKey)` (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:368) and passes it to CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan, which suppresses the clustered columnstore index whenever an identity primary key is present, because a clustered columnstore index cannot coexist with a clustered rowstore primary key (see target.columnStoreIndex).
keys.appliesWhen: Meaningfully creates an identity/primary-key column only on the run that CREATEs the target table.

keys.description: The target's three-part relational object name. See source.object for the full parsing description. The resulting RelationalObject also supplies the run-scoped staging table's database/schema (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:157-162 builds the staging object from flow.Target.Table.Database/.Schema) and is the table the canonical indexes (see target.columnStoreIndex), the truncate step (see target.truncateBeforeLoad), and the match-key/upsert scripts run against.

keys.appliesWhen: target.connection is set (ignored when target.server is used instead)

keys.validation: Unrecognized token: "<source>: 'target.provider' has unknown provider '<value>'. Allowed: mssql, azdb, mysql, postgres, oracle." A recognized non-SQL-Server kind fails via target.server's SQL-Server-only check.

Resolved into the synthetic connection name 'target' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.TargetConnectionName). The resolved target connection IS restricted to SQL Server, since the upsert is generated T-SQL.

Once resolved, a non-SQL-Server connection fails with "<source>: the target connection '<name>' is '<kind>'; an ingestion flow's target must be SQL Server (mssql or azdb)." (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:174-176, RequireSqlServerConnection, called from src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:95).

keys.description: Alias for 'target.object'; consulted only when 'object' is blank or absent. Same alias mechanics as source.table (any validation error still names the field 'target.object', never 'target.table').

Truncates the target table immediately before staging is applied, for full-reload semantics (legacy 'TruncateTrg' column, IngestionFlow.cs:31 comment). Bound via `targetYaml.TruncateBeforeLoad ?? false` (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:166) onto IngestionTarget.TruncateBeforeLoad. When true, IngestionFlowRunner emits and executes `TRUNCATE TABLE [schema].[table];` (two-part, schema-qualified, since the connection is already scoped to the target database) as run step 6 (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:396-402): after staging is filled and the target schema is evolved (and, on a create, after the canonical indexes and any SCD2 key index are applied), but before the keyed upsert / insert-all apply step. Unlike target.columnStoreIndex, target.identityColumn, and source.dataSetColumn (all consequential only on the run that creates the target), this flag is read and acted on EVERY run: any run with truncateBeforeLoad true wipes the table's rows immediately before every load, not just the first. The TRUNCATE statement carries no `IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NOT NULL`-style guard, unlike the rest of the engine's DDL/DML in this runner (DropStagingAsync's `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`, the canonical indexes' `IF NOT EXISTS`, EvolutionDdlGenerator's `IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NULL`); so if `schema.sync` is off and the target has never been created, this statement fails against a nonexistent table. That failure is still caught by RunAsync's outer handler (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:602), so the run ends gracefully as `IngestionRunResult { Success = false }`, but `Error` carries the raw underlying SqlException text (e.g. an 'Invalid object name' message) rather than a curated SqlFlowException/FlowValidationException message the way most anticipated engine failures are reported. Cross-validated at parse time against SCD2 (see validation): 'versioning.scd2.enabled: true' cannot combine with this flag, because SCD2 appends a new dated version per change and a truncate would erase that whole history.
keys.validation: `versioning.scd2.enabled: true` combined with `target.truncateBeforeLoad: true` is rejected at parse time: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' cannot be combined with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad'; truncating would erase the dimension history." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:133-137, only reached when versioning.scd2.enabled is true). No other validation on the key itself (a plain YAML bool).
keys.appliesWhen: Applies on every run where the flag is true, not gated to the run that creates the target, unlike target.columnStoreIndex / target.identityColumn / source.dataSetColumn. On the very same run that creates the target the TRUNCATE is a harmless no-op against the just-created empty table.

keys.default: { temporalHistory: false, insertUnknownDimensionRow: false, tokenVersioning: false, tokenRetentionDays: null, scd2: { enabled: false, validFromColumn: ValidFrom_DW, validToColumn: ValidTo_DW, currentFlagColumn: IsCurrent_DW, trackedColumns: [] } }
keys.description: Optional target-history block for a relational ingestion flow (flowType: ing). Binds to IngestionVersioningYaml and is mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVersioning into SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.VersioningPolicy, carried on IngestionFlow.Versioning (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionFlow.cs:77) through the whole run. Of its three direct boolean flags (temporalHistory, insertUnknownDimensionRow, tokenVersioning), one direct integer (tokenRetentionDays), and one sub-block (scd2), only 'scd2' has engine behavior today: 'temporalHistory' and 'insertUnknownDimensionRow' are rejected when set to true, and 'tokenVersioning'/'tokenRetentionDays' are parsed and stored but read by no engine code. When the 'versioning' key itself is absent, MapVersioning still runs and returns the all-off default policy (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:380-383).

Would insert an unknown-member row for dimension handling (legacy InsertUnknownDimRow). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: per the model's doc comment, a correct implementation needs a defined sentinel-key convention plus exemption from the match-key delete pass (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionPolicies.cs:203-206), so a flow that sets it to true is rejected rather than silently doing nothing. It is rejected twice: at YAML load, so an authored flow never gets further, and again at run time by IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures, which guards flows assembled through the other loaders (full-mode control-DB, legacy migration) that do not go through this YAML loader (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:205, 837-841).

Run time, for flows not built via this loader (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:837-841): SqlFlowException "insertUnknownDimensionRow is not yet implemented. Remove the flag; an unknown-member row must be seeded explicitly for now (a designed implementation with match-key exemption is pending)."

keys.default: { enabled: false, validFromColumn: ValidFrom_DW, validToColumn: ValidTo_DW, currentFlagColumn: IsCurrent_DW, trackedColumns: [] }
keys.description: Application-managed slowly-changing-dimension Type 2 (period-based) target history: the engine keeps a validity period per business-key row instead of overwriting it, so unlike 'versioning.temporalHistory' the feature can be turned on for an already-created, already-populated target (the period columns are added through ordinary schema evolution, and every pre-existing row is backfilled as the current version the first time the flow runs with it on). Binds to IngestionScd2Yaml and is mapped, with validation, by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapScd2 into SqlFlow.Core.Ingestion.Scd2Policy. Consumed by three collaborators once 'enabled' is true: IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds the three period columns to the target's desired schema, UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements replaces the plain two-step upsert with a backfill, close, and insert load, and CanonicalIndexPlanner turns the business-key index into a filtered unique index. When the whole 'scd2' key is absent, MapScd2 returns the disabled default without running the distinct-name check below, since it never computes candidate names to check. The legacy/full-mode row mapper (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/Legacy/IngestionFlowMapper.cs:136-142) never sets this sub-object at all, so today 'versioning.scd2' is reachable only by authoring the YAML flowType: ing document; a full-mode or legacy-sourced flow always gets the disabled Scd2Policy default.
keys.validation: The three period-column names below (each independently defaulted first) must be pairwise distinct, case-insensitively, whenever the 'scd2' block itself is present, regardless of 'enabled' (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:402-413): FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')."

keys.description: The current-row indicator column: 1 for the live version of a key, 0 for an expired one. When 'versioning.scd2.enabled' is true, IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds it to the target's desired schema (not the staging table, which the production runner builds through a separate, simpler column projection) as a nullable 'bit' system-role column, skipping the add if a same-named column already exists (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109, AddComputed at 148-163). At run time UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements sets it to 1 on backfilled rows and newly-inserted current versions, clears it to 0 when closing a changed current row, and uses 'trg.[column] = 1' as the anti-join condition that finds keys needing a new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:301, 308, 321-329, 355-362). It is also the filter predicate of the migrated business-key index: on every run where scd2 is enabled, not only the run that creates the target, IngestionFlowRunner calls CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements, which drops a same-named 'NCI_KeyColumn' that is not already a filtered unique index, drops any other non-filtered unique nonclustered index whose columns are exactly the business key, and creates 'CREATE UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [NCI_KeyColumn] ON <target> (<keyColumns>) WHERE [<currentFlagColumn>] = 1' (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:70-126, called from src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393). On the run that creates the target, CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan also uses 'versioning.scd2.enabled' itself (not this column) to suppress the plain, non-filtered unique 'NCI_KeyColumn' it would otherwise emit (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:36-40).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true for any schema or SQL effect; the value is still parsed and validated for distinctness even when enabled is false or the key is absent from an otherwise-present scd2 block
keys.validation: Blank or whitespace falls back to the default (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:404, NullIfBlank). Together with validFromColumn and validToColumn it must be pairwise distinct: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:402-413).

keys.description: Turns on the SCD2 load path. Off (the default), a keyed flow always applies through the plain two-step upsert. On, UpsertGenerator.GenerateStatements dispatches to GenerateScd2Statements instead (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:179-182), and 'load.skipUpdateExisting'/'load.skipInsertNew' are not consulted at all, because the SCD2 statement set replaces both plain branches entirely, per the UpsertOptions.Scd2Enabled doc comment (UpsertGenerator.cs:93-96); 'load.batchUpsert' and 'load.batchUpsertRowCount' (BatchToAvoidLockEscalation) are likewise never applied to the SCD2 statements, only to the plain and dataset-partitioned-loop paths, since GenerateStatements returns from the SCD2 branch before reaching that logic. The business key used by the SCD2 statements, and by the canonical or filtered index, is the flow's effective key columns (load.keyColumns, overridden by matchKeys.keyColumns when load.matchKeysInSourceAndTarget is also on), computed by IngestionFlowRunner.EffectiveKeyColumns (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:817-820, 903-926); this can differ from the plain 'load.keyColumns' count that the load-time validation below inspects. On the run that creates the target, CanonicalIndexPlanner.Plan suppresses the plain unique 'NCI_KeyColumn' index when this flag is on (CanonicalIndexPlanner.cs:36-40); on every run where it is on, IngestionFlowRunner additionally reconciles the key index to the SCD2 filtered-unique form via CanonicalIndexPlanner.Scd2KeyIndexStatements (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:382-393), which is how enabling SCD2 on a pre-existing table migrates its key index before the load can insert a second version of a key.
keys.validation: Load time, enforced only when true (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:123-138): the flow's own 'load.keyColumns' (not a matchKeys.keyColumns override) must be non-empty, else FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' requires 'load.keyColumns' (the business key the dimension versions by)."; 'target.truncateBeforeLoad: true' is forbidden, else FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' cannot be combined with 'target.truncateBeforeLoad'; truncating would erase the dimension history." Not checked at YAML load time, but enforced at run time when the flow also sets 'load.dataSetColumn' (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:152-157, reached from IngestionFlowRunner.BuildLoadStatements when the flow runs): SqlFlowException "A dataset-column load (DataSetColumn) cannot be combined with SCD2 versioning."

keys.default: [] (empty means every comparable non-key data column, the usual dimension behavior)
keys.description: SOURCE column names whose change opens a new dimension version; a change in any other column leaves the current row untouched. IngestionFlowRunner maps each entry to its cleaned TARGET name through the same source-to-target name map used for 'change.ignoreColumnsInHash', silently dropping any entry that is not a real bulk-copied column (for example one named in source.ignoreColumns, or a virtual column), before passing the mapped list to UpsertGenerator as Scd2TrackedColumns (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:893-896, 921). Inside UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements, a non-empty mapped list is intersected with the target's non-key data columns; an empty list instead falls back to every column already eligible for the plain change-detection checksum (every non-key column whose type supports HASHBYTES/CONCAT and that is not in change.ignoreColumnsInHash). Either way, columns excluded from the checksum are removed from the tracked set, and if nothing remains comparable the close statement is skipped entirely, so only brand-new keys get inserted and no existing current row is ever closed (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:282-289, 306-329).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true; when false the list is still parsed but IngestionFlowRunner never reads it (scd2Tracked is forced to an empty list, IngestionFlowRunner.cs:894-896)

keys.description: One SOURCE column name to track for SCD2 change detection. A blank or whitespace-only entry is filtered out while mapping the YAML list (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:421, NullIfBlank inside MapScd2); a non-blank entry that does not resolve to a bulk-copied target column, because it names an ignored or virtual column, is filtered out at run time instead of erroring (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:895, MapNameOrNull). Neither case raises a validation error; see 'versioning.scd2.trackedColumns' for how the resulting set is used.

The period-start column name. When 'versioning.scd2.enabled' is true, IngestionSchemaBuilder.AddScd2Columns adds it to the target's desired schema as a nullable 'datetime2(3)' system-role column, skipping the add if a same-named column already exists (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109, AddComputed at 148-163); being nullable is what lets the ALTER TABLE ADD succeed on an already-populated target. Final column position is rank-based, not add-order-based: IngestionSchemaBuilder.Order buckets every column into Rank 0 (name starts with 'PK'), Rank 1 (ends with 'PK'), Rank 2 (ordinary), or Rank 3 (ends with '_DW'), sorts by rank first, and only breaks ties within the same rank by the column's original build-order index. A name (default or overridden) ending in '_DW' falls into Rank 3, so it sorts after every ordinary (Rank 2) column, including the real source/virtual data columns. A custom name that does NOT end in '_DW' instead falls into Rank 2, the same rank as an ordinary source column, so it sorts BEFORE all '_DW' columns (not after them); within that Rank-2 group it lands after the real source/virtual columns, because AddScd2Columns appends it to the internal column list after they were added (IngestionSchemaBuilder.Order and Rank, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:168-192). At run time UpsertGenerator.GenerateScd2Statements both reads and writes it: the backfill statement sets it, for any target row whose period is still NULL, to the existing value if present, else InsertedDate_DW when that system column is on, else the epoch '1900-01-01 00:00:00.000'; the insert statement sets it to the run's single as-of instant (captured once per run so a closed row's ValidTo equals the new row's ValidFrom exactly) for every new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:278, 293-303, 333-342).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true for any schema or SQL effect; the value is still parsed and validated for distinctness even when enabled is false or the key is absent from an otherwise-present scd2 block
keys.validation: Blank or whitespace falls back to the default (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:402, NullIfBlank). Together with validToColumn and currentFlagColumn it must be pairwise distinct: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:402-413).

keys.description: The period-end column name; the current version of a key holds the open-ended sentinel '9999-12-31 23:59:59.999' (the maximum datetime2(3) value, UpsertGenerator.Scd2OpenSentinel, src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:260), so every point-in-time query over the dimension is a uniform half-open ValidFrom-to-ValidTo range with no NULL special case. Added to the target's desired schema the same way as validFromColumn: a nullable 'datetime2(3)' system-role column, skipped if already present (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:100-109); the same Rank-based column-ordering rule applies (see 'versioning.scd2.validFromColumn'). At run time: the backfill statement stamps it with the open sentinel for any row whose period is NULL; the close statement stamps it with the run's as-of instant on a current row (flag equal to 1) whose tracked attributes changed from the staged row; the insert statement stamps it with the open sentinel on every new current version (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:293-303, 305-329, 333-342).
keys.appliesWhen: versioning.scd2.enabled: true for any schema or SQL effect; the value is still parsed and validated for distinctness even when enabled is false or the key is absent from an otherwise-present scd2 block
keys.validation: Blank or whitespace falls back to the default (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:403, NullIfBlank). Together with validFromColumn and currentFlagColumn it must be pairwise distinct: FlowValidationException "<source>: 'versioning.scd2' validFromColumn, validToColumn, and currentFlagColumn must be three distinct names (got '<validFrom>', '<validTo>', '<current>')." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:402-413).

keys.description: Would maintain a SQL Server system-versioned (temporal) history table for the target (legacy trgVersioning). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: per the model's doc comment, system-versioning interacts with the schema-evolution engine and is treated as a dedicated, not-yet-built feature (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionPolicies.cs:197-200), so a flow that sets it to true is rejected rather than silently ignored. It is rejected twice: at YAML load, so an authored YAML flow never gets further, and again at run time by IngestionFlowRunner.EnsureSupportedFeatures, which runs before any connection is opened and guards flows assembled through the other loaders (full-mode control-DB, legacy migration) that skip this YAML loader (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:205, 830-835).

Use 'versioning.scd2' for engine-managed dimension history." Run time, for flows not built via this loader (IngestionFlowRunner.cs:830-835): SqlFlowException "versioning.temporalHistory (SQL Server system-versioned history) is not yet implemented. Use versioning.scd2 for engine-managed dimension history, which works on an existing populated target."

keys.description: Reserved (legacy TokenRetentionDays). Parsed straight through with no coalescing, 'TokenRetentionDays = y.TokenRetentionDays' (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:390), and carried on VersioningPolicy.TokenRetentionDays (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionPolicies.cs:213), but read by no engine code found in this codebase: it is not consumed by IngestionFlowRunner, UpsertGenerator, IngestionSchemaBuilder, or CanonicalIndexPlanner. Paired in the model's doc comments with 'tokenVersioning' for a future token-retention feature.

Reserved (legacy TokenVersioning, which the model's doc comment notes the legacy engine itself logged as not implemented). Parsed and carried on VersioningPolicy.TokenVersioning for fidelity with the legacy row (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionPolicies.cs:208-210), but read by no engine code: unlike temporalHistory and insertUnknownDimensionRow it is not rejected when set, and unlike scd2.enabled it triggers no schema or SQL generation. Setting it currently has no observable effect on a run.

Computed projection-column declarations (a faithful port of legacy flw.IngestionVirtual rows), bound to List<IngestionVirtualColumnYaml> (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/IngestionYaml.cs:37) and mapped by YamlIngestionFlowLoader.MapVirtualColumns (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:425-448) into IngestionFlow.VirtualColumns (IReadOnlyList<VirtualColumn>, src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/IngestionFlow.cs:66). Consumed entirely by IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-76): it builds a name -> declaration lookup from every entry with a non-blank name (case-insensitive; when the list has duplicate names, only the FIRST declaration for that name is kept, IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-43), then walks the flow's INTROSPECTED SOURCE columns. A source column whose RAW (pre-schema.cleanColumnNames) name matches a declaration is re-marked Role=Virtual/Origin=Computed, its projection becomes that declaration's expression instead of the raw bulk-copied value, and it is excluded from the source-to-target bulk-copy name map, so it is neither read from the source nor treated as a data column for the upsert (though it still appears, computed, in the built target/staging schema). A declaration whose name matches no introspected source column, or that has no name at all, is never looked up and so silently contributes nothing to the built schema -- it is not an error. Because a virtualized column is excluded from the bulk-copy map, naming it (directly, or via matchKeys/versioning.scd2 resolving to it) as a key column fails schema-evolution's canonical-index planning with SqlFlowException "Key column '<name>' is not a bulk-copied target column (is it in IgnoreColumns or a virtual column?)." (IngestionFlowRunner.MapName, src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Ingestion/IngestionFlowRunner.cs:1157-1161) and fails upsert generation itself with "Key column '<name>' is not among the data columns." (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Schema/UpsertGenerator.cs:143).

One computed-column declaration; binds IngestionVirtualColumnYaml {name, dataType, dataTypeExpression, expression} (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/IngestionYaml.cs:170-176) and maps to a VirtualColumn record (src/SqlFlow.Core/Ingestion/VirtualColumn.cs:7-21). Only expression is required; name, dataType, and dataTypeExpression are all optional and blank/whitespace values normalize to unset.
keys.validation: An entry missing expression fails with FlowValidationException "<source>: 'virtualColumns[<i>].expression' is required." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:436-437).

keys.description: The declared target SQL type (legacy DataType, e.g. nvarchar(50)), bound onto VirtualColumn.DataType for round-trip fidelity with the legacy flw.IngestionVirtual.DataType column. Not read anywhere in the V3 engine path found in this repository: IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build ignores it entirely and always keeps the matched source column's own introspected SQL type (optionally narrowed by schema.convertUnicodeToNonUnicode) for a virtualized column (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:52,59). Currently has no effect on the generated schema, upsert, or transformation view.

A T-SQL expression documented as yielding the column's type (legacy DataTypeExp, e.g. CAST('2022-01-01' AS DATE)), an alternative to dataType; bound onto VirtualColumn.DataTypeExpression for legacy flw.IngestionVirtual parity. Like dataType, it is not read anywhere in the V3 engine path found in this repository (IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build never references it); currently has no effect on the generated schema, upsert, or transformation view.

The T-SQL select expression producing the column's value (legacy SelectExp; VirtualColumn.SelectExpression). When the entry's name matches an introspected source column, IngestionSchemaBuilder substitutes this expression as that column's SqlColumn.SelectExpression in place of the raw bulk-copied value (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:54-63); the resulting column nonetheless keeps the matched SOURCE column's own SQL data type (after any schema.convertUnicodeToNonUnicode narrowing), NOT a type derived from this entry's own dataType or dataTypeExpression (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:52,59).
keys.validation: Missing, null, empty, or whitespace-only throws FlowValidationException "<source>: 'virtualColumns[<i>].expression' is required." (YamlIngestionFlowLoader.cs:436-437).

keys.default: unset (null); an entry with no name is never looked up, so it never affects the built schema
keys.description: The output column name (legacy ColumnName; VirtualColumn.Name). IngestionSchemaBuilder.Build matches it case-insensitively against the RAW (pre-cleanup) name of each introspected source column, not the cleaned/target name (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-54); only a source column whose raw name matches is turned into this declaration's computed projection. When the virtualColumns list declares the same name more than once (case-insensitively), only the first declaration for that name is used; later duplicates are silently ignored (IngestionSchemaBuilder.cs:40-43).
